Hi Hannah,

We observed a sustained 503/error spike across multiple endpoints between ~09:05 and 09:28 UTC this morning in eu-west-2. Our customers reported failed tokenization calls and checkout retries; overall success rate dropped to ~68% for that window. Attached is a small snippet of our edge logs showing 503 responses and the pattern we saw (acme-503-snippets.txt).

Can you confirm if this maps to a Redwood service outage or a routing/third-party problem? We need an official downtime window for our invoicing and for an SLA credit claim. If possible, please provide: 1) confirmed downtime start/end (UTC), 2) severity classification, and 3) whether this is eligible under the SLO/SLA for pro-rata credits.

We appreciate a quick acknowledgement and an ETA for a postmortem. Our legal and finance teams are waiting on the formal window to start internal credit paperwork.

Thanks — Alicia

Hannah / team — initial telemetry (edge + serving runtime) shows a correlated spike in 5xx for model routing between 09:04:50 and 09:26:47 UTC. Two observations:

1) There was a degraded routing decision when the primary pool for eu-west-2 hit transient CUDA OOM on a small subset of hosts; the runtime retried to a slower quantized variant which caused increased latency and a backlog leading to propagated 503s at the gateway.
2) Total affected traffic for Acme's routes appears to be ~52% of requests during the window (their mix of tokenization + chat calls hit the faulty hosts).

I’ve exported a timeline we can attach to the claim: incident-timeline-euw.csv (contains minute-by-minute success rate and routing events). Based on current thresholds (SLA: 99.9% uptime monthly per region), this window looks likely to qualify for a pro-rata credit. Final classification requires SRE confirmation on host-level remediation timestamps and whether this meets the "service unavailability" definition in our SLA.

Action items:
- Jonas: please confirm host remediation and provide exact host reboot/rollout end times.
- Hannah: please coordinate provisional credit reservation with finance and let Acme know the expected formal window.

Karthik
Head of Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-01T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: 503 spike — eu-west-2 (09:05–09:28 UTC) — please confirm downtime window

Karthik / Hannah — host-level info:
- Root cause: a buggy autoscaler loop during a burst (minor memory leak in our custom allocator) caused 7 hosts in the eu-west-2 primary pool to exceed host memory thresholds and trigger eviction/restarts.
- Remediation: rolling restart completed and traffic rebalanced by 09:27:12 UTC. Last host reported healthy at 09:26:58 UTC.
- Impact window (observed at infra layer): 09:04:52 UTC -> 09:27:12 UTC.

I recommend we mark the official downtime window as 09:05:00 — 09:27:12 UTC to be conservative (round start to next clean second and end to remediation completion).

Jonas
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
